form.label: Routes
form.description: The jumps a permitted flow has actually been seen to make: from a declared entry point to a host, from that host onward, and what is listening where it lands.

search.query: | `riskability_fw_edges` | stats count AS edges | append [| inputlookup riskability_netevidence_lookup | stats count AS ledger, count(eval(coverage_state="no firewall data")) AS nofw] | stats max(edges) AS edges, max(ledger) AS ledger, max(nofw) AS nofw | eval edges = coalesce(edges, 0), ledger = coalesce(ledger, 0), nofw = coalesce(nofw, 0) | eval state = case(edges == 0 AND (ledger == 0 OR nofw == ledger), "unconfigured", edges == 0, "empty", 1=1, "ready")

div.b: No firewall data source has been configured, so there are no routes to draw.
div.span: This page draws the jumps a permitted flow has been seen to make, from the firewall's own logs. Nothing here is measured on the hosts, so without a firewall source the app cannot say anything about the network and shows nothing rather than guessing. Exposure on the other pages is unaffected: it is measured from how each process bound its socket.

An administrator configures the source in Riskability Configuration, Firewall data source: the index and field names, and the entry points (the internet, an admin network) that a route can start from. Until then every Network evidence row reads unknown, which is correct.

div.b: A firewall source is configured, but it yielded no permitted edges in the last 30 days.
div.span: Either the source holds no permitted flows yet, or the field mapping does not match the events. An administrator can run Test source on the Firewall data source page to see which. Nothing is drawn until an edge exists, because an empty graph and a quiet network look the same.

viz.option: Edges exist, but none from a declared entry point has resolved to a host and port in the inventory. Either no entry point is declared, or the addresses the firewall logged are not ones the inventory has seen a host hold. The Network evidence page's "where the app refused to name a host" panel says which.

div.span: CVE-enabled: a jump a CVE alone can make
needs a foothold: reachable, but wants credentials or a click
unrated: an open finding has no CVSS vector
permitted only: needs a zero-day or permissions
host reachable from an entry point on CVEs alone

div.b: A jump here is a permitted flow the firewall logged, and its colour is what an attacker would need to take it.
div.span: Every jump is graded from the open findings on the software listening where it lands, using the CVSS vector: reachable over the network with no privileges and no user action is CVE-enabled; reachable but wanting credentials or a click needs a foothold; and a flow onto a listener with nothing usable over the network is permitted only, which means the jump needs a zero-day or permissions the firewall knows nothing about. A red ring marks a host an attacker can reach from an entry point on CVE-enabled jumps all the way; the first jump of any other colour is where the CVE-only path stops. Widths are sessions on the left and open CVEs on the right; a thin edge is still a path. CVE-enabled means possible, not proven: nothing here was exploited.

panel.title: Every path from an entry point, and what each jump needs

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_netevidence_lookup | where observed_grade IN ("confirmed observed", "historically observed") | eval rk_entry = mvindex(split(coalesce(entry_text, "entry point"), " "), 0) | search rk_entry=$entry_filter|s$ | stats values(rk_entry) AS rk_entries BY hostname, port | mvexpand rk_entries | eval src = rk_entries, dst = hostname, hop = 1 | fields src, dst, hop, port | append [ | `riskability_fw_edges` | lookup riskability_hostaddr_lookup address AS src_ip OUTPUT hostname AS rk_src_host, claimants AS rk_src_claim | lookup riskability_hostaddr_lookup address AS dest_ip OUTPUT hostname AS rk_dst_host, claimants AS rk_dst_claim | where isnotnull(rk_src_host) AND isnotnull(rk_dst_host) AND rk_src_host != rk_dst_host | where mvcount(rk_src_host) == 1 AND mvcount(rk_dst_host) == 1 | where coalesce(tonumber(rk_src_claim), 1) <= 1 AND coalesce(tonumber(rk_dst_claim), 1) <= 1 | stats count BY rk_src_host, rk_dst_host, port | eval src = rk_src_host, dst = rk_dst_host, hop = 0 | fields src, dst, hop, port ] | eval port = replace(tostring(port), "\.0+$$", "") | eventstats values(eval(if(hop >= 1, dst, null()))) AS rk_h1 | eval hop = if(hop == 0 AND isnotnull(mvfind(rk_h1, "^" . src . viz.option: No path starts at a declared entry point. A path needs a permitted flow from an entry point to a host the inventory knows, and this graph has none.

div.b: A path is CVE-enabled as far as its jumps stay red; the stop is the first jump that needs more.
div.span: Each jump is graded by the best open finding on any port the flow reached on the next host, so a path's grade is as generous as the weakest listener on the way. "Needs a zero-day or permissions" means the firewall allowed the traffic and nothing open at the far end is usable over the network: an attacker would need something the app does not know about. A path that is CVE-enabled all the way is still a possibility, not a demonstrated route.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_findings_state_lookup where status="open" | eval rk_sel = $sel_node|s$, rk_kind = replace($sel_kind|s$, "^\d+:", "") | eval rk_host_of_port = if(rk_kind == "port", mvindex(split(rk_sel, ":"), 0), null()) | eval rk_port_of_port = if(rk_kind == "port", mvindex(split(rk_sel, ":"), 1), null()) | eval rk_cve_host = if(rk_kind == "cve", trim(mvindex(split(mvindex(split(rk_sel, " @ "), 1), " › "), 0)), null()) | eval rk_cve_pkg = if(rk_kind == "cve", trim(mvindex(split(mvindex(split(rk_sel, " @ "), 1), " › "), 1)), null()) | where case(rk_kind == "host", hostname == rk_sel, rk_kind == "package", package == rk_sel, rk_kind == "cve", hostname == rk_cve_host AND package == rk_cve_pkg, rk_kind == "port", hostname == rk_host_of_port, 1=1, false()) | lookup riskability_exposure_lookup hostname, package OUTPUT port AS rk_ports | where rk_kind != "port" OR mvfind(rk_ports, "^" . rk_port_of_port . "$") >= 0 | join type=left hostname [ | inputlookup riskability_netevidence_lookup | where observed_grade IN ("confirmed observed", "historically observed") | stats values(port) AS rk_observed_ports BY hostname ] | eval rk_port_one = if(rk_kind == "host", rk_ports, "n/a") | mvexpand rk_port_one | eval rk_behind_observed = if(rk_kind != "host", 1, if(isnotnull(rk_observed_ports) AND isnotnull(mvfind(rk_observed_ports, "^" . rk_port_one . "$")), 1, 0)) | where rk_behind_observed == 1 | dedup finding_key | lookup riskability_aiverdicts_lookup cve_id OUTPUT priority_tier, priority_score, recommended_action, rationale | `riskability_cvss_reach` | eval "Over the wire" = case(rk_rank == 3, "yes, no foothold needed", rk_rank == 2, "yes, but needs credentials or a click", rk_rank == 1, "no CVSS vector", 1=1, "no, local only") | eval Tier = coalesce(priority_tier, "P" . case(severity=="critical", 1, severity=="high", 2, severity=="medium", 3, 1=1, 4)) | eval Score = coalesce(priority_score, ""), KEV = if(isnotnull(kev_added) AND kev_added != "", "yes", "") | eval Fix = coalesce(fixed_version, "") | eval "Why" = coalesce(rationale, "not analysed by the pipeline yet; tier from severity") | sort 0 - rk_rank, Tier, - Score | eval Installed = coalesce(current_version, last_version) | rename hostname AS Host, package AS Software, cve_id AS CVE, severity AS Severity, recommended_action AS Action | table Tier, Score, CVE, "Over the wire", Severity, KEV, Host, Software, Installed, Fix, Action, "Why"

viz.option: No open finding sits behind this point. For a host that means nothing open is behind a port traffic was observed to reach; for a port, nothing open on the software listening there.

div.b: Every row is an open finding the app already holds; nothing here is computed from the firewall.
div.span: The route says traffic was permitted to this point. These are the findings that were open on the software listening there, with the pipeline's tier where it has analysed them and a tier from severity where it has not. Over the wire reads the CVSS vector: the attack vector, whether privileges are needed, and whether a user has to act. A row that says "no foothold needed" is the one that makes a jump CVE-enabled; the rest sit behind the jump without opening it. A host click lists only the findings behind ports traffic was observed to reach, not everything open on the machine. Clicking an entry point narrows the graph to it instead, since an entry point has no findings of its own.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_netevidence_lookup | search hostname=$host_filter|s$ | where observed_grade IN ("confirmed observed", "historically observed") | eval From = coalesce(entry_text, ""), To = hostname . ":" . port, Kind = "entry point to host" | eval rk_entry = mvindex(split(coalesce(entry_text, "entry point"), " "), 0) | search rk_entry=$entry_filter|s$ | eval rk_src = "__entry__", rk_dst = hostname, hop = 1 | fields From, To, Kind, observed_grade, sessions, srcs_text, edge_last_seen, rk_src, rk_dst, hop | append [ | `riskability_fw_edges` | lookup riskability_hostaddr_lookup address AS src_ip OUTPUT hostname AS rk_src_host, claimants AS rk_src_claim | lookup riskability_hostaddr_lookup address AS dest_ip OUTPUT hostname AS rk_dst_host, claimants AS rk_dst_claim | where isnotnull(rk_src_host) AND isnotnull(rk_dst_host) AND rk_src_host != rk_dst_host | where mvcount(rk_src_host) == 1 AND mvcount(rk_dst_host) == 1 | where coalesce(tonumber(rk_src_claim), 1) <= 1 AND coalesce(tonumber(rk_dst_claim), 1) <= 1 | search rk_src_host=$host_filter|s$ OR rk_dst_host=$host_filter|s$ | stats sum(sessions) AS sessions, max(edge_last_seen) AS edge_last_seen, values(src_ip) AS srcs_text BY rk_src_host, rk_dst_host, port | eval From = rk_src_host, To = rk_dst_host . ":" . port, Kind = "host to host", observed_grade = "lateral, permitted" | eval rk_src = rk_src_host, rk_dst = rk_dst_host, hop = 0 | fields From, To, Kind, observed_grade, sessions, srcs_text, edge_last_seen, rk_src, rk_dst, hop ] | eventstats values(eval(if(hop == 1, rk_dst, null()))) AS rk_h1 | eval hop = if(hop == 0 AND isnotnull(mvfind(rk_h1, "^" . rk_src . "$$")), 2, hop) | eventstats values(eval(if(hop == 2, rk_dst, null()))) AS rk_h2 | eval hop = if(hop == 0 AND isnotnull(mvfind(rk_h2, "^" . rk_src . "$$")), 3, hop) | eventstats values(eval(if(hop == 3, rk_dst, null()))) AS rk_h3 | eval hop = if(hop == 0 AND isnotnull(mvfind(rk_h3, "^" . rk_src . "$$")), 4, hop) | eventstats values(eval(if(hop == 4, rk_dst, null()))) AS rk_h4 | eval hop = if(hop == 0 AND isnotnull(mvfind(rk_h4, "^" . rk_src . "$$")), 5, hop) | where hop > 0 | eval Kind = if(hop == 1, Kind, "host to host, hop " . hop) | eval "Last seen" = if(isnotnull(edge_last_seen) AND edge_last_seen != "", strftime(tonumber(edge_last_seen), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), "") | eval Sources = mvjoin(mvdedup(srcs_text), " ") | rename observed_grade AS Grade, sessions AS Sessions | sort hop, - Sessions | table Kind, From, To, Grade, Sessions, Sources, "Last seen"

viz.option: No jump has been observed from a declared entry point, and no permitted host-to-host flow resolved to two inventory hosts.
